examShortTricks: Trick 1: Sacks's argument: libraries are sanctuaries of learning and community, not mere book warehouses — state his thesis and one memory he uses.
Trick 2: His personal anecdotes (childhood library, the Willesden library's fate) carry the emotion — structure answers around two anecdotes.
Trick 3: The closing plea: saving libraries = saving learning itself — link his closing to a modern threat (digital closure, funding cuts).
practiceQuestions: Q. Why does Sacks value libraries? (2 marks) — they gave him knowledge, refuge and community as a child and young scientist.
Q. What does the closure of a library mean to a community? (2 marks) — loss of free access to knowledge and a shared civic space.
keyPoints: Libraries shaped Sacks as a scientist and writer — personal memory as argument.
Physical books vs digital: he defends the sensory, serendipitous library experience.
